label: Foundational beings are necessary at w, from power grounding
meaning: PGP's verdict at the foundational case. Take a being f foundational at w and a world v accessible from w; excluded middle decides whether f exists at v. Were f absent there, it would be contingent at w, and PGP would make it corruptible simply or put it under some being's power over its esse; the foundational profile excludes both, each by its own clause (incorruptibility for POSSIBLE_NOT_TO_BE_1, the no-power clause for POSSIBLE_NOT_TO_BE_2). So f exists at every accessible world. No step passes from one sense of 'possible not to be' to the other: the sense bridge names PGP as the premise in which both occur, as alternative channels. Only the profile's actuality, incorruptibility and no-power clauses are used: simplicity, unreceivedness, firstness and uncausedness are idle here (under correlation, the no-power clause itself follows from uncausedness and incorruptibility, controls law 1).

strong_version_needed.ee4ab504-c8fe-59bc-bc96-7cbeefed6410: The proof applies excluded middle to propositions outside LocalLogic's scope, e.g. `F.history.ontic.ExistsAt v f`. LocalLogic (ca432e24) decides only whether an actual bearer is identical with a GOD_4 candidate, and gives double-negation elimination for that candidate's esse–essence identity.
